Step 8 is complete.

## What I did

Adjudicated all **327 rejections** across **223 items** from `research/frontier-12-judge.jsonl`, reading every rejected item in full and opening cited sources wherever a lane alleged a Fact overstated its dependency.

**First check that mattered:** all 454 items' `item_sha256` match current disk, and both lanes judged byte-identical text. So no judge saw pre-step-6 text — the dispatch's "if a judge raises a step-6 finding it's a false positive" escape never applied.

## Outcomes

| | rows |
|---|---|
| `confirmed_fatal` | 6 (3 items) |
| `false_positive` | 4 |
| `confirmed_nonfatal` | 317 |

**Three fatal defects, repaired — and two of the three were introduced by my own step-6 repairs:**

- `lem-green-type-i-boundary-identity` / `lem-green-type-ii-boundary-identity` — step 1.2 asserted α(a)=β(a) at the endpoints. The region definition requires α<β only on the *open* interval, so a **rectangle** is a Type I region with strict endpoint inequality. My step-6 note read "permits α=β" as "requires". Both lanes, same counterexample. Replaced with the real case split; the Green conclusions were never wrong (endpoints are measure-zero in the outer integral).
- `cor-potentials-differ-by-a-componentwise-constant` — [L1] ended with "a set is piecewise-C¹ path-connected exactly when it is one such class", which is false ((0,1) ⊆ ℝ). Also mine, from step 6. Corrected to the true direction, which is the one both consumers actually need.

The other 317 rows are citation-fidelity and 30-second gaps — the judges were told to check local licensing only, which generates that class en masse. I closed them without touching a byte. §5 of the report names the six I'd fix at step 6 of a future touch, including a tautological proof route in `lem-homomorphisms-respect-commutators-and-derived-series` and a triangle identity the published definition explicitly denies in `prop-equivalences-preserve-…-limits-and-colimits`.

## Two corrections to flag

**A ledger-contract trap:** `judge.mts` and `tools/item-hash.mjs` normalize differently (judge strips only the `judge:` sub-block; the guard strips all of `verification:`). My first ledger used the judge value and `step8-guard` correctly rejected all three repairs as `nonfatal-edit` despite the fatal rows being present. Rebuilt with `itemContentHash`, every row verified against the `pre-step8` baseline before writing. Guard now: **3/3 licensed**.

**I ran `level-coverage --verify-current-context` rather than deferring it, and it is not green.** Beyond my 3 expected `judge-coverage-missing` errors, it surfaced two **pre-existing** blockers my step-6 gate table missed: the audit receipt has `plan_reconciliation: []` against 14 items with real dep drift, and **this run has no spine receipt at all** (`frontier-12-spine*` doesn't exist; every prior run has one). Neither is step-8 work and I haven't fabricated either — but the level is **not** ready for step 9 on the strength of the rejudges alone.

Gates otherwise green: precheck, depcheck, fwdcheck, extcheck, rendercheck, prosecheck, `proof-contract --strict` 370/370, finite-smoke, `risk-report --require-reviewed`, impact-audit (1 interface, both consumers read — no change needed).

Report: `research/frontier-12-alpha-step8.md`. Rejudge set: the three ids above.
